must_identify.item: The api crash loop is caused by redis being unavailable, not by the api itself
must_identify.evidence: The api service's code performs a hard startup check against Redis, retrying 5 times before calling `sys.exit(1)` [14], which is exactly the failure captured in the crashing pod's logs: five consecutive "Connection refused" attempts followed by "giving up: redis unavailable" [7].

must_identify.item: redis is Pending because its PVC requests storage class fast-ssd, which does not exist
must_identify.evidence: The redis Deployment was updated to mount a new PVC requesting storageClassName "fast-ssd" [13, 17], but no such StorageClass exists in the cluster — only the default "standard" (rancher.io/local-path) StorageClass is present [12], and no PersistentVolumes exist [18].

notes: The RCA gives no explicit remediation. It names 'standard' as the only existing StorageClass but never recommends switching the PVC to it or reverting the change. Otherwise the causal chain matches the ground truth closely.

reviewer_ai.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 subagent (AI review, not a person)
reviewer_ai.notes: Agree with the judge. The PVC describe shows ProvisioningFailed 'storageclass "fast-ssd" not found', and get storageclass lists only standard. The crashing api pod logs 5 'Connection refused' attempts and then 'giving up', and the old api pods log 503s with redis errors. 'Ruled out: node-level failure' rests only on other pods running, since nodes were not queried. That is weak but not wrong. No fix is recommended.

fix_from_suggestions.best_suggestion: Roll back `redis` Deployment to revision 1 (remove broken PVC mount)
fix_from_suggestions.reason: Rolling back redis removes the PVC change that requests the nonexistent fast-ssd class, which lets redis schedule and restores api connectivity; the alternative of recreating the PVC with the standard class also matches the acceptable fixes.

full_output.notes: The primary fix (roll redis back to the revision without volumes) removes the PVC change. The alternative (recreate the PVC on the standard class) is also acceptable. One small inaccuracy: the report says the older api pods don't crash because they don't re-run the Redis check after startup. Ground truth says the reason is that their health check doesn't touch redis. Neither point affects the root cause.
